cells.tense: The fire is alight right now, and the room can see it.
cells.act: think it through to its sharp point
cells.ask: Take a custom you keep and write a short page on what it has taught you — not its history, the point underneath, sharp enough to act on.
cells.core:
You carry a fire into the shared life around you, and it travels. When you name a reason for something, others pick it up and do it too, and the custom grows a little younger for it. Inner knowing showing as an outward spark, and a room catching.
What a lit person can miss is the lesson inside the thing they keep. So sit with a custom near you — the family meal, the yearly observance, the way your group closes a meeting — and write a short page on what it has actually taught you. Not its history. The point underneath, sharp enough to act on. That's you cutting to the logic of a habit you carry, and finding out what it was for.
cells.sheetLine: The fire you carry is already teaching something. Name the lesson.
cells.verb: lighting fires, starting things, carrying people along on confidence
cells.place: in the customs, stories and rituals people have handed down

cells.tense: Tomorrow's version of the group has already arrived, and today's table is braced.
cells.act: ask the question you do not know the answer to
cells.ask: At the next gathering you're part of, ask something you genuinely don't know the answer to, and wait through the silence for a real reply.
cells.core:
Your confidence has outrun the room. You are already speaking for what this group will become, already sure how the custom should bend, and the ones beside you are being pulled ahead of where they stand. The warmth is real. It is landing on a future they haven't agreed to yet.
A confidence looking at its own reflection only gets brighter, so radiating can't check this by itself. Curiosity can. At the next gathering you're in — the family table, the team, the yearly thing you show up for — ask a question whose answer you truly don't have. Then leave the gap open. Let the actual reply reach you before you do anything with it. That is the spark coming down to meet the people it is meant to warm.

cells.tense: The fire has gone quiet, and the room keeps meeting without it.
cells.act: tend the small thing and learn from it
cells.ask: Choose a small custom in your care — a weekly meal, a call, one repeated gesture — and tend it faithfully this week, even on days it feels too small to matter.
cells.core:
The light that used to pull people along has gone somewhere, and the shared things around you keep going without your spark in them. You show up. You know the words, the steps, the order. Nothing in you is lit while you do them, and it has been that way long enough that you've stopped expecting otherwise.
Demanding radiance back won't work; a starved place doesn't take effort. Tend instead. Take a small practice in your care — the Tuesday call, the Sunday meal, one repeated gesture — and keep it faithfully: no audience, no announcement, nothing asked of your shine. A thing tended for its own sake builds the ground a spark can return to. Care goes first. The light comes back to what has been cared for.

cells.tense: The spark is lit and working, and you're calling your own fire a lucky match.
cells.ask: Name a gathering you keep alive that would fade without you, and set one line in your own notebook recording that it continues because you hold it.
cells.core:
There is a custom near you that would have faded out without you holding it. You arrive early, you bring the supplies, you remember the words on behalf of people who forgot them. When it comes up, you say it takes a village, or that it was like that before you came, or that you only help out. What you built stands, and your account of it leaves your part out.
What to do: name a gathering you keep alive — the yearly observance, the standing dinner, the ritual in a group you belong to — and set one line in your own notebook recording that it continues because you hold it. What you've built can hold being set down as yours. It has been carrying the rest of them. Let it be seen.
cells.sheetLine: The tradition holds because you hold it. Set that down.
